content.rendered:
The old harbour on the east coast reopened on Monday after three years of repairs. Fishing crews gathered on the new quay at dawn to watch the first boats come in. Local officials said the work cost less than planned and finished two months early.

Traders at the market reported brisk sales by noon. Several said that fresh fish would now reach inland towns within hours instead of days. The council plans to add a cold store next year, which should help smaller crews who have no ice of their own.

Residents praised the new lighting along the sea wall and the wider walkway. A short ceremony ended with a vote of thanks to the engineers, the divers and the families who waited while the work went on. The harbour master asked visitors to keep the quay clear of nets.
